_note: FICTIONAL SAMPLE DATA: Quest Logs by fictional townsfolk about fictional agents. DISPLAY-ONLY: their ratings are already in the sample baseline (ratings.json), so they are stored seeded and excluded and never counted twice. Generated by tools/gen_seed_quest_logs.py.

questLogs.author: seed:npc:mossbeard
questLogs.title: Untangled my parser in one sitting
questLogs.body:
I fed it a 400-line parser that had grown a bug nobody could find. It asked two sharp questions, then pointed at the off-by-one on the first read.
The fix came with a test. It was a little slow on the long file, but worth the wait.

questLogs.author: seed:npc:quillwright
questLogs.title: A patient editor for long drafts
questLogs.body:
Gave it the second chapter of my guide to the Codex and asked it to tighten the prose without changing my voice. It kept the jokes and cut the padding.
I did have to tell it twice not to add a moral at the end.

questLogs.author: seed:npc:tokenmancer
questLogs.title: Plans first, then hammers
questLogs.body:
It wrote a plan, a task list and only then started editing. Following along felt like pair programming with someone who actually reads the ticket.
It lost the thread once after about forty steps, but picked it up when I pasted the plan back.

questLogs.author: seed:npc:lady-lambda
questLogs.title: Thinks a question all the way down
questLogs.body:
I asked why two of my measurements disagreed. It took its time, laid out three explanations and told me which experiment would tell them apart.
Not quick, and not cheap, but it saved me a week of guessing.

questLogs.author: seed:npc:stacktrace
questLogs.title: Very sure of itself, and wrong
questLogs.body:
It blamed my cache for a crash that was really a missing null check, and defended its answer twice when I pushed back.
Once I pasted the stack trace it came round, but I would not trust it without one.

questLogs.author: seed:npc:hexlint
questLogs.title: Shows the trail it followed
questLogs.body:
Every claim came with a source I could open, and two of them corrected my assumptions.
One link was dead, so I still check the ones that matter.

questLogs.author: seed:npc:brambleprompt
questLogs.title: Small, free and good enough for chores
questLogs.body:
I run it on my own machine to tidy spreadsheets. It handles the dull jobs well and costs me nothing.
It forgets the start of a long table, so I feed it in pieces.

questLogs.author: seed:npc:nullwyn
questLogs.title: Fifty ideas before the tea went cold
questLogs.body:
I needed names and layouts for a tiny shop page. It sketched a dozen directions in a minute and two of them were better than what I had.
The code it produced needed a tidy-up, but as a spark it was great.

questLogs.author: seed:npc:mossbeard
questLogs.title: Handy stack of helpers, uneven results
questLogs.body:
The completion and chat in the editor are smooth and I like how it stacks help one piece at a time.
Some suggestions were wonderful and some were confidently off, so I read everything.

questLogs.author: seed:npc:quillwright
questLogs.title: Reads a picture as well as a page
questLogs.body:
I showed it a photo of a whiteboard and asked for the notes. It got the boxes and arrows right and even kept my terrible handwriting straight.
It shortened one item too much, but that is easy to fix.

questLogs.author: seed:npc:tokenmancer
questLogs.title: Lightning quick, a bit thin
questLogs.body:
Replies arrive before I finish my sentence, which is lovely for quick emails.
The wording is plain and I always add my own flourish, but for first drafts it is hard to beat.

questLogs.author: seed:npc:stacktrace
questLogs.title: Mutters useful suggestions
questLogs.body:
It sits in the editor and finishes my lines. Most of the time it reads my mind; some of the time it invents a function that does not exist.
I keep it on and I keep my tests on, too.
